beats: Equivalence pH is 7 for strong with strong, above 7 for a weak acid with strong base, and below 7 for a weak base with strong acid.
Pick an indicator whose range sits on the steep part near the equivalence pH. Volume to equivalence depends on moles, not acid strength.
Polyprotic acids show one equivalence point per proton.

beats: Rest near -70 mV (close to EK, set by K^+ leak). Threshold near -55 mV starts a positive feedback loop of Na^+ channel opening.
Na^+ rushes in, the voltage heads toward ENa (+61 mV) but peaks lower.
Na^+ channels inactivate and slow K^+ channels open, so K^+ leaves and the cell repolarizes, then undershoots toward EK.
Inactivated Na^+ channels cause the absolute refractory period; lingering K^+ current causes the relative one. Myelin and wide axons speed conduction.
action-potential-phases-ion-channels.title: Action Potential Phases and Ion Channels, Step by Step

beats: Backbone groups are about pKa 2 and 9 to 10.
Acidic side chains are around 4, histidine around 6, cysteine near 8, tyrosine near 10, lysine near 10.5, arginine near 12.5.
Pass a pKa going up in pH and the charge drops by one. The pI is the average of the two pKa values around the neutral species.
At pH 7.4, Asp and Glu are negative, Lys and Arg are positive, and almost everything else is neutral or a zwitterion with no net charge.
amino-acid-pka-charge-ph-7-4.title: Amino Acid pKa Values and Charge at pH 7.4

beats: Epimers differ at exactly one stereocenter; anomers differ only at the anomeric carbon formed on ring closure (C1 of aldoses, C2 of ketoses).
D-mannose is the C2 epimer and D-galactose the C4 epimer of D-glucose; mannose and galactose are plain diastereomers.
D-glucose and L-glucose are enantiomers; glucose and fructose are constitutional isomers.
In a D-sugar Haworth ring, alpha puts the anomeric OH opposite the CH2OH and beta on the same side.
anomers-vs-epimers-carbohydrates.title: Anomers vs Epimers: Carbohydrate Stereoisomers for the MCAT

beats: Watch the exceptions: intracellular bacteria, wall-less *Mycoplasma*, giant viruses, prions and viroids.
A bacterium has everything a cell needs.
Bacterial genomes all follow the same rule as ours: double-stranded DNA is copied by DNA polymerase, transcribed into RNA and translated on ribosomes.
Bacteria reproduce by binary fission.
bacteria-vs-viruses-differences.title: Bacteria vs Viruses: Structure, Replication and Treatment

beats: Continuity: Q = Av is constant, so narrowing a pipe speeds the flow, and speed scales with 1/r².
Bernoulli: P + ½ρv² + ρgh is constant along a streamline for an ideal fluid, each term an energy per volume in pascals.
At constant height, faster flow means lower static pressure (Venturi effect). At constant speed, higher means lower pressure by ρgΔh.
With the fluid at rest it becomes the hydrostatic equation, and for a hole in an open tank it gives Torricelli's v = √(2gh).
bernoulli-equation-continuity-venturi.title: Bernoulli's Equation and the Venturi Effect for the MCAT

beats: Pyruvate dehydrogenase converts pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, CO2 and NADH in the matrix. Per turn: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, 2 CO2, worth about 10 ATP.
Per glucose, the whole pathway yields roughly 30 to 32 ATP. ATP and NADH inhibit; ADP and Ca^2+ activate.
Pyruvate from glycolysis is carried into the matrix and converted by the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH):
Track carbon counts as you go.

beats: Classical: stimulus-stimulus link, involuntary response, cue before US. Terms: US, UR, NS, CS, CR.
Operant: behavior-consequence link, voluntary behavior, consequence after behavior.
Positive means add, negative means remove. Reinforcement increases, punishment decreases.
Escape and avoidance are negative reinforcement. Shaping rewards successive approximations.
classical-vs-operant-conditioning.title: Classical vs Operant Conditioning: Differences, Terms and Examples

beats: Colligative properties depend on particle count. Raoult's law: P = XsolventP°. Osmotic pressure Π = iMRT uses molarity and kelvin.
The van't Hoff factor is 1 for nonelectrolytes, 2 for NaCl, 3 for CaCl2, and real values run slightly lower. To rank solutions, compare i × m.
Here R = 0.0821 L atm/(mol K) and T must be in kelvin. ΔTf and ΔTb are written as positive sizes of the shift.
you then subtract from the normal freezing point or add to the normal boiling point.

beats: Conformity: matching peers, no explicit demand. Obedience: following an authority's command.
Asch: about one third of critical answers conformed. roughly 75 percent of people gave in at least once. plateau near three or four confederates.
one ally sharply cuts it.
Normative influence: wanting acceptance, public only. Informational: believing others know better, can change private belief (Sherif).

beats: Stage 1: high births, high deaths, slow growth.
Stage 2: deaths fall first, births stay high, rapid growth, expansive pyramid.
Stage 3: births fall, growth slows.
Stage 4: low births and deaths, near-zero growth, column-shaped pyramid.

beats: Four Ds: deviance, distress, dysfunction, danger. Diagnosis needs the criteria plus distress or impairment.
DSM-5 dropped the multiaxial system, split bipolar from depressive disorders, and moved OCD and trauma out of anxiety.
DSM-5-TR's newest diagnosis: prolonged grief disorder.
Psychosis by duration: under 1 month brief psychotic, 1 to 6 months schizophreniform, 6 months or more schizophrenia.
dsm-5-psychological-disorders-categories.title: DSM-5 Categories of Psychological Disorders for the MCAT

beats: Learn the reaction pattern first and the name clues second, and double-check the odd ones: phosphorylase, synthase vs. synthetase, and dehydratase.
Each enzyme gets a four-part number: EC a.b.c.d.
Reaction: transfer of electrons (or hydrogen atoms) from one molecule to another.
Reaction: transfer of a functional group (phosphate, amino, methyl, acyl, glycosyl) from a donor to an acceptor.

beats: Eight stages, birth to old age, each a crisis between two poles with a virtue as the healthy outcome.
Infancy trust (hope), toddler autonomy (will), preschool initiative (purpose), school-age industry (competence).
Adolescence identity (fidelity), young adulthood intimacy (love), middle age generativity (care), late life integrity (wisdom).
Identity must precede intimacy. Marcia's four identity statuses expand stage 5.

beats: Functionalism: macro, society as interdependent parts, stability. Durkheim, Parsons, Merton. Manifest vs latent functions, dysfunctions.
Conflict theory: macro, groups compete for scarce resources, inequality and change. Marx, Weber (class, status, party), Dahrendorf, Mills.
Symbolic interactionism: micro, meanings built in interaction. Mead, Blumer, Cooley, Goffman.
Looking-glass self, dramaturgy, Thomas theorem, labeling.
functionalism-vs-conflict-theory-vs-symb.title: Functionalism vs Conflict Theory vs Symbolic Interactionism

beats: Dispositional = person. Situational = circumstances.
Fundamental attribution error: others' behavior gets too much dispositional explanation.
Actor-observer bias: self explained by situation, others by disposition. Driven by perspective.
Self-serving bias: my success is me, my failure is the situation. Driven by self-esteem.
fundamental-attribution-error-vs-actor-o.title: Fundamental Attribution Error vs Actor-Observer vs Self-Serving Bias

beats: Galvanic: spontaneous, E positive, ΔG negative, anode negative, cathode positive.
Electrolytic: driven by a supply, E negative, ΔG positive, anode positive, cathode negative.
In both, oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode, electrons through the wire from anode to cathode, cations toward the cathode.
Use E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode, ΔG = -nFE, and E = E° - (0.0592/n) log Q at 25 C.
galvanic-vs-electrolytic-cells.title: Galvanic vs Electrolytic Cells: Signs, Electron Flow and Examples

beats: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. Negative means spontaneous, positive means the reverse is favored, zero means equilibrium.
With ΔH negative and ΔS positive the process is always spontaneous; with the opposite signs, never. Convert J to kJ and use kelvin.
The second law says a process is spontaneous when the total entropy of the universe rises: ΔSuniverse = ΔSsystem + ΔSsurroundings > 0.
ΔH and ΔS are each either positive or negative, so there are four cases.
gibbs-free-energy-delta-g-spontaneity.title: Gibbs Free Energy: Delta G, Spontaneity and Temperature

beats: Ten cytosolic steps convert glucose to 2 pyruvate.
Investment phase: hexokinase and PFK-1 each spend 1 ATP, and aldolase plus triose phosphate isomerase give 2 G3P.
Payoff phase, twice per glucose: GAPDH makes NADH, phosphoglycerate kinase and pyruvate kinase each make ATP. Net 2 ATP, 2 NADH, 2 pyruvate.
Without oxygen, lactate dehydrogenase regenerates NAD^+.

beats: p + q = 1 and p² + 2pq + q² = 1.
Equilibrium assumes no mutation, no migration, no selection, random mating and a large population, and serves as a null model for evolution.
Start from q² (the recessive phenotype, or 1 minus the dominant phenotype), take the square root, then find p and 2pq.
With genotype counts, count alleles. For X-linked recessive traits, affected males = q and affected females = q².

For added strong acid or base, do the mole bookkeeping first. In blood, pH = 6.1 + log([HCO3^-]/(0.03 × PCO2)).

Each ionizable group on an amino acid obeys the same equation with its own pKa.

Bonds to H sit high (above 2700), triple bonds near 2100 to 2260, C=O near 1650 to 1800, and C-O near 1000 to 1300.

beats: The lac operon (CAP site, promoter, operator, lacZ, lacY, lacA) makes one mRNA for the lactose genes.
The repressor, made constantly from lacI, blocks the operator until allolactose binds it.
CAP-cAMP, present when glucose is low, activates the weak promoter.

beats: v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]). Km is the substrate concentration giving half of Vmax. Low Km usually means high affinity. Vmax = kcat[E]total.
On a Lineweaver-Burk plot the y-intercept is 1/Vmax, the x-intercept is -1/Km, and the slope is Km/Vmax.
Imagine a fixed amount of enzyme and a growing amount of substrate.

beats: Mitosis: one division, two identical daughters, same ploidy, sisters separate at anaphase.
Meiosis: one replication, two divisions, four different haploid cells.

Meiosis II separates sister chromatids (equational) and looks like mitosis.

beats: Filtration: net pressure about 10 mmHg, GFR about 125 mL/min (180 L/day), proteins and cells stay in the blood.

Thick ascending limb: NaCl out, watertight, filtrate dilutes, medulla concentrates to about 1200 mOsm/L.
Distal tubule: NaCl (thiazides) and Ca^2+ (PTH).

beats: P50 (about 26 to 27 mmHg in adults) is the PO2 at half saturation, and a higher P50 means lower affinity.

beats: Passive: down the gradient, no energy. Simple diffusion for small nonpolar molecules, linear and unsaturable.

Secondary transporters spend the Na^+ gradient (symport such as SGLT1, antiport such as the Na^+/Ca^2+ exchanger).

beats: Balance every nuclear equation by conserving A and Z separately. Alpha: A drops 4, Z drops 2. Beta-minus: Z up 1.
